clearing_status.fact: The SEC granted one formal one-year extension on Feb 25, 2025 (Release No. 102487), moving cash compliance to Dec 31, 2026 and repo to Jun 30, 2027. As of Aug 7, 2026 (Commissioner Uyeda SEC statement), those dates remain current with no second extension announced, but SIFMA exemptive-relief requests published Apr 17, 2026 remain pending (comment deadline Aug 31, 2026). Sources: https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/press-releases/2025-43; https://www.sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/uyeda-statement-update-secs-work-toward-treasury-clearing-implementation-080726-update-secs-work-toward-treasury-clearing-implementation-august-2026
clearing_status.rationale: Rubric 1 is satisfied on two independent grounds: an official extension was granted (Feb 2025) and SIFMA exemptive-relief requests remain pending as of Aug 2026. No second formal extension has been identified, so rubric 2 does not apply.

plan_financing.fact: Japan 10-year JGB yield reached 2.99% on Sep 11, 2026 (Trading Economics / MoF), up ~15bps from the Sep 1 auction stop of 2.840% and cumulatively >50bps above mid-2026 levels, driven by Takaichi fiscal-stimulus concerns and BOJ rate-hike expectations; the Sep 1 10-year auction cleared at a yield of 2.995% with no reported failed bid-to-cover or emergency BOJ operation; Takaichi's May supplementary budget promised no new net bond issuance but her food-tax-cut financing path remains unspecified (CNBC, Aug 4 2026).
plan_financing.rationale: The 10-year yield is materially elevated on fiscal concern (cumulative rise well above 25bps) and the financing path for the consumption-tax cut is unspecified, satisfying the UNCLEAR criteria; however, no auction has failed (bid-to-cover <2) and no emergency BOJ operation has been documented, so the DISORDERLY threshold is not met.

dissent.view: Lazard (Jun 2026) notes Takaichi has actively tempered fiscal stimulus expectations to reassure bond markets, implying the yield rise is as much BOJ normalisation-driven as fiscal-shock-driven, which would soften the fiscal-stress reading toward 0.

direct_lending_default.fact: Fitch Ratings reported today (September 14, 2026) that the trailing 12-month US private credit default rate rose to 6.3% at end of August 2026, a new record surpassing the prior month's 6.1%, per Bloomberg citing Fitch's report released Monday. Source: https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-14/us-private-credit-default-rate-hits-a-record-of-6-3-fitch-says
direct_lending_default.rationale: Fitch's inclusive TTM measure (counting distressed exchanges and maturity extensions) printed 6.3% for August 2026, eclipsing the prior record of 6.1% in July and the April 2026 record of 6.0%; this is the mandated anchor per the rubric and no anchor switch is required as a fresh Fitch print is available. The rate trajectory (5.6% Dec-2025 → 5.8% Jan → 6.0% Apr → 6.1% Jul → 6.3% Aug) signals sustained and accelerating credit deterioration in private direct lending, consistent with elevated PIK income at BDCs and maturity-extension-dominated default events.

dissent.view: Proskauer Private Credit Default Index (count-based, senior secured/unitranche only) reported 2.51% for Q2 2026 across 716 loans representing $195.6B — roughly 3.8 points below Fitch's inclusive rate
Moody's estimated 2025 private credit headline default rates of 1.6%–4.7% excluding distressed exchanges, with distressed restructurings accounting for ~65% of all 2025 private credit defaults
IMF April 2026 Global Financial Stability Report described private credit default rates in the 2–3% range as 'manageable in magnitude'

redemption_gates.fact: Fitch Ratings data (cited by multiple trade sources as of Aug 17 2026) shows 10 of 16 tracked BDCs breached their 5% quarterly repurchase caps in Q2 2026; named funds with active gates include Blackstone BCRED (~$79B AUM, gated Jun 4 2026), Blue Owl OTIC (38.1% request rate, paid ~12 cents on dollar), Cliffwater CCLFX (~$31B, 17% requests vs 5% honored), Apollo Debt Solutions BDC (~$26B, 11%+ requests), and Morgan Stanley North Haven Private Income Fund (~$7B, 11.6% requests). R.A. Stanger pegs Q2 requests at 12.4% of NAV industry-wide, with only 38% fulfilled and ~$9.6B left unmet.
redemption_gates.rationale: The rubric threshold for level 2 is >=3 of the largest funds gating, or combined AUM >$100B; at least 5 named large funds—including BCRED ($79B) and Cliffwater CCLFX ($31B) alone exceeding $100B combined—hit their quarterly repurchase caps in Q2 2026, with 10/16 Fitch-tracked BDCs breaching caps in the same quarter, far exceeding the widespread threshold.

dissent.view: iCapital (Mar 2026) argued funds were honoring 100% of tenders even when requests exceeded 5%, characterising the episode as sentiment-driven rather than structural; early Q3 data (Golub GCRED cleared July tender in full at 4.8%) suggest some easing in Q3 2026

new_imf_programs.fact: In the trailing 6 months (Mar–Sep 2026): Bolivia reached a staff-level agreement for a new EFF on Jul 29 2026 (IMF.org PR, awaiting Board approval); Kenya formally requested a new IMF program after abandoning its 9th review under the existing ECF/EFF (Reuters/Yahoo Finance, 2026); no Board-approved brand-new sovereign programs or confirmed missed coupon/standstill events were found in the window. Existing programs for Argentina (2nd review, May 21 2026) and Ukraine (1st review, Jul 20 2026) are ongoing reviews, not new arrangements.
new_imf_programs.rationale: One to two sovereigns (Bolivia SLA, Kenya new-program request) entered new-distress-program territory in the window, with no confirmed missed coupons; this is consistent with RISING (1-2 new IMF arrangements) rather than CALM or CLUSTER.

dissent.view: Bolivia SLA is not yet Board-approved; Kenya has only submitted a request with no approval—stricter reading could argue 0 new formally approved programs, implying CALM (0)

china_ppi.fact: China PPI for industrial products rose +3.8% year-on-year in August 2026, per NBS release dated 9 September 2026 (Xinhua: 'China's producer price index (PPI)...went up 3.8 percent year on year in August, the National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) said Wednesday'). PPI also rose +0.4% month-on-month. Source: https://english.news.cn/20260909/08bda30608aa431e9c6f830a7deced63/c.html and https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/09/china-cpi-ppi-august-oil-prices-tech-manufacturing-.html
china_ppi.rationale: At +3.8% YoY, China PPI is in positive cost-push territory — not deflation, but a moderate positive reading. The rubric scores on SIZE of move; +3.8% is a notable positive print reflecting upstream commodity and energy price pressure with potential to export input-cost inflation to trading partners.

trade_actions.fact: In the trailing 3 months (Jun 14–Sep 14 2026), at minimum 6 major new measures were enacted or formally proposed: (1) USTR 12.5% Section 301 forced-labor tariff on broad Chinese goods, eff. Jul 24 (China Briefing/Congress.gov CRS, Jul 2026); (2) US proposed 7.5% overcapacity tariff on China, Bloomberg Aug 24 2026; (3) China 54.3% provisional anti-dumping on US pecans, MOFCOM Aug 11 2026; (4) China drone export controls + 6 US entity bans, MOFCOM Aug 5 2026; (5) China preliminary anti-dumping on Japanese chip chemical (DCS), MOFCOM Sep 8 2026; (6) US Commerce AD/CVD determination on Chinese L-lysine + spray-foam circumvention inquiry, Federal Register Jul 23-24 2026. EU AD duties on Chinese ceramics also raised to 79% in mid-2026.
trade_actions.rationale: The 3-month count stands at >=6 discrete new measures across multiple major economies (US, China, EU), including a broad Section 301 tariff covering all Chinese goods at 12.5% — itself a wide-sector action — and a second broad overcapacity tariff proposed at 7.5%; this satisfies both the '>=4 new measures' and 'broad tariff round >=10% across a sector' thresholds of Level 2 (ESCALATING).

dissent.view: Some trackers note a Xi-Trump summit expected in September 2026 and bilateral trade talks ongoing, suggesting managed escalation rather than full breakdown; Bloomberg Aug 24 framed the overcapacity tariff as pre-summit positioning, not a truce rupture.

license_flow.fact: As of September 2026, China's April 2025 MOFCOM export licensing regime (Announcement No. 18) remains fully in force for seven medium/heavy rare earth elements and downstream magnets (NdFeB containing Dy/Tb, SmCo). Licensing is case-by-case per shipment; general licences exist but are available only to a small whitelist of named Chinese producers (e.g. JL MAG, Zhongke Sanhuan, Ningbo Yunsheng, issued Dec 2025) and are not broadly available. Processing times routinely run 60–120 days in practice, well above the 45-working-day statutory target. The January 2026 Export Licensing Catalogue added samarium, gadolinium, and lutetium compounds as new controlled categories. The October 2025 expansion (extraterritorial/0.1% rule) remains suspended until 10–27 November 2026 under MOFCOM Announcements No. 70/72 (2025). Sources: gettransport.com logistics guide (Jul 7 2026); rare-earth-mining.com buyer guide (Apr 16 2026); certivo.com (Mar 11 2026); techtimes.com (May 27 2026).
license_flow.rationale: The regime is case-by-case per shipment for most exporters, general licences are whitelisted to named producers only (not broadly available), processing times routinely exceed 30 days (60–120 days observed), and new categories (samarium, gadolinium, lutetium compounds) were added to the control list within the trailing 3 months of the Jan 2026 catalogue update — all three rubric triggers for Score 1 (SLOWING) are met. Score 2 is not warranted because licences are still being issued across civilian/automotive end-users and no categorical denial or formal suspension of licensing has been announced.

dissent.view: Rare Earth Exchanges (Apr 2026) cites licensing approval rates below 25% for European firms in some sectors, which some analysts read as approaching a functional freeze for those buyers — closer to Score 2 for defence/advanced-tech applicants.

truce_status.fact: MOFCOM Nov-7-2025 suspension of Oct-9 rare-earth controls remains in force until Nov 10, 2026 (primary: whitehouse.gov fact-sheet Nov-5-2025; MOFCOM Announcements 70/72). However, on June 22, 2026, China added 10 US entities — including MP Materials and USA Rare Earth — to its export control list (MOFCOM, benchmarkminerals.com, bloomberg.com, June 22 2026). As of Sep 14 2026, the expiry is <60 days away with no renewal announced (moderndiplomacy.eu, Aug 21 2026).
truce_status.rationale: The truce is formally unextended with <60 days to its Nov-10-2026 nominal expiry and a confirmed partial breach (entity-specific export-control additions on June 22, 2026) satisfying the rubric-1 'fraying' condition; blanket controls have not been reimposed (ruling out 2), but the muted market signal from entity listings is consistent with partial rather than full breach.

dissent.view: Entity-list additions are 'largely symbolic' as targeted firms have little commercial exposure to China, and the blanket suspension is intact — some analysts read this as still holding at 0
Modern Diplomacy (Aug 21 2026) frames the truce as 'increasingly resembling a pause' with Beijing unlikely to extend, suggesting trajectory toward 2

re_blacklist.fact: MOFCOM Announcement No. 23 of 2026, issued 22 June 2026, added 10 named US entities to China's export control list; the two US rare-earth producers explicitly named are MP Materials Corp. and USA Rare Earth, Inc. The other eight entities are defense/drone/aerospace firms (Aveox, Red Cat Holdings, Teal Drones, IMSAR, Jaia Robotics, Ball Aerospace, Oshkosh Defense, L3Harris Maritime Services). The measure is firm-specific, not a categorical ban on the US rare-earth sector. Sources: MOFCOM Announcement No. 23 of 2026 as reported by GlobalSecurity.org (citing Global Times, 22 Jun 2026); Benchmark Minerals (25 Jun 2026); Bloomberg (22 Jun 2026); Al Jazeera (22 Jun 2026).
re_blacklist.rationale: Two named US rare-earth producers (MP Materials Corp. and USA Rare Earth, Inc.) appear on the MOFCOM export-control list by firm name, not as a sector class, mapping directly to rubric value 1. Benchmark Minerals explicitly characterises the measure as 'entity-specific rather than a blanket restriction on rare earth exports to the US', and market price signals were described as muted, consistent with a firm-specific rather than sector-wide action.

hree_premium.fact: Dysprosium oxide trades at $205–211/kg inside China vs $575–$1,100+/kg ex-China (floor-to-spot range), implying a 2.7x–5.2x multiple; Argus data cited by Reuters (June 2026) and REEx (Aug 6, 2026) characterise the dysprosium/terbium ex-China premium as '4x to 5x' domestic Chinese prices. Benchmark Minerals (March 24, 2026) reported 2025 dysprosium CIF North America at 4.4x EXW China. Sources: rareearthexchanges.com (Aug 6 2026), theoregongroup.com citing Argus/Reuters (June 10 2026), source.benchmarkminerals.com (March 24 2026).
hree_premium.rationale: Multiple corroborating sources from mid-to-late 2026 converge on a 4x–5x ex-China premium for the canonical HREE benchmark (dysprosium oxide); 4.5 is the midpoint of that observed range and is supported by both Argus price data and Benchmark Minerals' 2025 baseline of 4.4x trending higher into 2026.

genius_impl.fact: The GENIUS Act Section 13 statutory rulemaking deadline was July 18, 2026. As of that date and through at least mid-August 2026, zero agencies (OCC, FDIC, Federal Reserve, NCUA, Treasury, FinCEN, OFAC) had issued final implementing rules — every workstream remained at the NPRM/proposed stage. Treasury published a further NPRM on stablecoin issuance in August 2026 with comments due October 19, 2026 (Federal Register, 2026-08-18). Sources: coinpaprika.com (July 19-20 2026), astraea.law (July 18 2026), federalregister.gov (August 18 2026), fdic.gov (April 2026 NPRM), occ.gov (NPRM bulletin 2026-3), home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0605.
genius_impl.rationale: The July 18, 2026 statutory deadline was missed with zero final rules published by any primary regulator — this maps squarely to rubric level 2 ('deadline missed without final rules'). The Act's effective date now defaults to the January 18, 2027 backstop, and Treasury continued issuing new NPRMs in August 2026 with comment periods running to October 2026, confirming no imminent finalization.

dissent.view: Paradigm and Chapman & Cutler note agencies face 'no formal penalties' for missing the rulemaking deadline and the GENIUS Act still takes effect January 18, 2027 via the 18-month backstop, suggesting operational continuity rather than a crisis scenario.
Astraea Counsel characterizes the missed deadline as a rulemaking slip, not an Act-effectiveness failure, since the January 18, 2027 statutory backstop remains intact.

ai_revenue_gap.fact: Q2 2026 actuals: Google Cloud +82% YoY to $24.8B (accelerating from +63% in Q1), AWS +37% YoY to $42.2B (accelerating from +28% in Q1), Azure +43% YoY. Combined 2026 hyperscaler capex raised to ~$725-740B (+77% YoY from ~$410B in 2025), with Amazon raising to ~$220B, Alphabet to $195-205B, Meta to $130-145B. Sources: company Q2 2026 earnings releases; Synergy Research Q2 2026; uncoveralpha.com (Aug 3 2026); fourweekmba.com (Jul 31 2026).
ai_revenue_gap.rationale: Capex growth (~77% YoY aggregate) exceeds AI-cloud revenue growth for AWS (+37%) and Azure (+43%), keeping the monetization gap WIDE. However, all three hyperscalers show QoQ acceleration in AI-revenue (Google Cloud 63%->82%, AWS 28%->37%), ruling out level 2 (WIDENING FAST), which requires deceleration or an outlook cut.

dissent.view: Google Cloud alone grew 82% YoY in Q2 2026, which exceeds the ~77% aggregate capex growth rate, suggesting the gap may be CLOSING for Alphabet specifically; Alphabet also raised capex ceiling to $205B at Q2 earnings, partially offsetting this.

Pre-Q2 analysis (July 20 2026) flagged that 'the buildout is accelerating faster than the monetisation curve' and cited Moody's May 2026 credit-risk warning if AI profit growth fails to materialise, a more bearish framing closer to level 2.

gpu_refi_stress.fact: On July 29, 2026, CoreWeave's 5-year CDS spread hit ~855 bps (implying ~50% default probability), a level associated with distressed borrowers; the company then had to sweeten terms to place a $2.6 billion leveraged loan tied to Anthropic. CoreWeave also carries a $4.2 billion pre-Meta refinancing wall due in 2026 on GPU-backed debt where collateral values have declined. No confirmed default or distressed exchange has occurred; Q2 2026 revenue beat at $2.1B+ and the $2.6B loan ultimately cleared. Sources: Bloomberg (2026-03-31, 2026-07-29), metirai.com/CDS analysis (2026-08-02), capacityglobal.com (2026-08-12), davefriedman.substack.com (2026-04-19).
gpu_refi_stress.rationale: CoreWeave is a named borrower facing a documented 2026 refinancing wall on GPU-backed debt with sharply widening CDS spreads (855 bps, distressed-tier), satisfying Rubric 1 ('a named borrower facing a refinancing wall'). No confirmed default, failed refinancing, or distressed exchange has been reported — the $2.6B loan cleared after sweetened terms — so Rubric 2 is not triggered.

dissent.view: CoreWeave's Q2 2026 revenue beat (+200% YoY, $104B backlog) and successful loan placement suggest refinancing stress is manageable and not acute; equity analysts maintain Buy ratings with ~$145 avg target.

cmbs_office_delinq.fact: Trepp CMBS office delinquency rate jumped 63 bps in October 2025 to set a new all-time high of 11.76% (source: commercialsearch.com/news/cmbs-delinquency-rates/, reporting Trepp data, published ~Nov 2025). The July 2026 overall Trepp CMBS rate surged to 7.86% (+51 bps) driven in part by a Chicago office tower and a Seattle office portfolio going delinquent, but a Trepp office-specific sub-rate for 2026 was not available in retrievable excerpts.
cmbs_office_delinq.rationale: The rubric requires the latest published Trepp CMBS office delinquency percent; the hardest confirmed Trepp office figure is 11.76% (Oct 2025 all-time high), with July 2026 Trepp data showing continued office stress but no office sub-rate extractable from available sources, yielding medium confidence. KBRA data for early 2026 (12.8%–13.9%) and S&P paywalled headline (>10.5% in Jan 2026) are consistent with an elevated but uncertain 2026 Trepp office rate. [vintage guard: new read is 2025-10 data but the prior applied value was 2026-03 data; kept the newer vintage]

dissent.view: KBRA office CMBS delinquency rate was 13.9% in January 2026, falling to 12.8% in February 2026 — materially higher than the Trepp figure, reflecting KBRA-rated universe differences and the One New York Plaza ($835M) maturity default event
S&P Global Ratings headline states the office CMBS rate 'surpasses 10.5%' in January 2026 (paywalled), implying a lower reading than KBRA under S&P's universe definition

regional_bank_stress.fact: FDIC failed-bank list (last updated 2026-08-21) shows exactly ONE bank failure in all of 2026: Metropolitan Capital Bank & Trust, Chicago, closed 2026-01-30, $261.1M assets. That failure falls outside the trailing-6-month window (2026-03-14 to 2026-09-14). Regulators cited 'unsafe and unsound conditions and an impaired capital position'; no official FDIC/OCC/Fed post-seizure analysis has named CRE concentration as the cause. Bisnow (2026-02-02) reported court records show a troubled real-estate-linked loan as a contributing factor, but this is credible press inference, not a formal supervisory determination. No coordinated interagency CRE enforcement action has been identified. Source: https://www.fdic.gov/bank-failures/failed-bank-list (updated 2026-08-21); https://www.bisnow.com/national/news/capital-markets/cre-tied-to-first-bank-failure-of-2026-133023 (2026-02-02).
regional_bank_stress.rationale: Zero FDIC bank failures in the trailing 6 months (March-September 2026) and no formal supervisory statement or enforcement action officially citing regional-bank CRE concentration satisfies the CALM rubric (score=0). The sole 2026 failure pre-dates the window and lacks an official CRE-cause determination, preventing elevation to ISOLATED.

dissent.view: Bisnow/The Real Deal (2026-02-02) infer CRE loan exposure as a material contributor to the Metropolitan Capital failure based on court records, which would support an ISOLATED reading if that failure were counted within the rubric window or if the CRE link were officially confirmed.

govt_stability.fact: The Second Lecornu government (incumbent, formed 10 Oct 2025) is a minority coalition governing without a working majority. It has survived multiple no-confidence votes — most recently on 2 Feb 2026, when two motions (far-left: 260 votes; far-right: 135 votes) fell well short of the 289 required, allowing the 2026 budget to pass. No dissolution or snap election has been called. Sources: Al Jazeera (2 Feb 2026 https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/2/2/france-adopts-2026-budget-after-two-no-confidence-votes-fail), Wikipedia Lecornu governments (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lecornu_governments), Euronews (23 Jan 2026 https://www.euronews.com/2026/01/23/french-government-avoids-collapse-after-surviving-two-no-confidence-votes).
govt_stability.rationale: Lecornu II holds no working majority and has repeatedly relied on Socialist/conservative forbearance to survive no-confidence votes — textbook rubric 1 (FRAGILE). No confidence vote has been lost and no dissolution called, so rubric 2 (COLLAPSE) does not apply.

rating_action.fact: S&P Global Ratings downgraded France from AA- to A+ with a stable outlook on 17 October 2025 (S&P press release; sourceId/101651950); Fitch Ratings separately downgraded France from AA- to A+ in September 2025 (Bloomberg, 2025-09-12); Moody's maintained Aa3 but revised outlook to negative on 24-25 October 2025. As of 28 August 2026, Fitch reaffirmed A+ / stable (Bloomberg, 2026-08-28).
rating_action.rationale: Two of the three major agencies (Fitch in Sep-2025, S&P on 17-Oct-2025) executed actual one-notch rating cuts on France within the trailing 12 months ending 2026-09-14, satisfying rubric band 2 (DOWNGRADE). Moody's negative outlook (Oct-2025) would independently satisfy band 1, but the executed cuts by Fitch and S&P set the highest applicable band.

dissent.view: Moody's did NOT downgrade; it only moved to negative outlook (Aa3/Negative, Oct-2025), which alone would be band 1, not band 2.
Fitch on 28 Aug 2026 reaffirmed A+ with STABLE outlook, suggesting no further deterioration since the Sep-2025 cut.

subprime_auto_dpd.fact: Fitch Ratings subprime auto ABS 60-day-plus delinquency rate in June 2026 was 5.67%, down 64 basis points year-over-year, per Wolf Street citing Fitch (published August 13, 2026).
subprime_auto_dpd.rationale: The Fitch ABS index is the primary authoritative source for this metric; 5.67% is the latest month (June 2026) with a hard reported figure, mapping directly to the rubric's request for the latest subprime auto 60+ day delinquency rate as a percent.

dissent.view: 5.49% in May 2026 (lowest since May 2024) per ankso.blog citing Fitch — slightly lower than June figure, possibly a May datapoint before seasonal uptick
6.80% in February 2026 per TradingEconomics/Fitch — earlier in the year before seasonal improvement

bnpl_delinq.fact: Affirm FQ3'26 Shareholder Letter (SEC 8-K, May 7 2026, period ending March 31 2026): '30+ day delinquencies excluding Peloton and Pay in X loans increased 29 basis points year over year ... to 2.8%'; allowance for credit losses 6.0% of loans held for investment; projected ultimate net charge-offs ~3.5% of cohort GMV, in-line with expectations. Klarna Q1 2026 credit-loss provisions 0.55% of GMV vs 0.54% YoY. Source: https://investors.affirm.com/static-files/5a0ae9e1-e495-4030-b115-b7d5a502e5e6
bnpl_delinq.rationale: Affirm 30+ DPD rose 29 bps YoY to 2.8% — above flat but well below the 100 bps spike threshold; projected charge-offs ~3.5% are below the 5% spiking threshold, fitting rubric level 1 (RISING, charge-offs contained). Klarna provisions are essentially flat YoY, providing no systemic escalation signal.

dissent.view: Benzinga/SahmCapital (June 2 2026) characterises Affirm 30+ DPD as 'flat against a year earlier at 2.8%', understating the +29 bps YoY move documented in the primary SEC filing

LendingTree survey (March 2026) puts 47% of BNPL users as having paid late in the past year (up from 41% in 2025 and 34% in 2024), a far harsher characterisation than lender balance-sheet data, but is a self-reported survey not a hard delinquency rate

dollar_reserve_share.fact: IMF COFER Data Brief (published ~June 30, 2026): 'The share of US dollar holdings in foreign exchange reserves increased to 57.13 percent in 2026Q1, from 56.42 percent in 2025Q4.' Source: https://data.imf.org/en/news/imf%20data%20brief%20july%201
dollar_reserve_share.rationale: The IMF COFER Q1 2026 release is the most recent official data point; 57.13% maps directly to the rubric requiring the latest USD share of allocated global FX reserves as a percent. The figure is confirmed by multiple IMF-sourced secondary outlets with no material deviation.

weaponization_event.fact: At the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi on 12 September 2026, BRICS leaders formally adopted BRICS Pay — a payment-messaging network integrating India's UPI, China's CIPS, Russia's SPFS, and Brazil's Pix — as a new non-dollar cross-border settlement layer (Eastern Herald, 12 Sept 2026). Separately, the EU's Dec 12 2025 vote made the ~€210-230bn Russian central bank asset freeze indefinite, but full confiscation/title transfer has not been executed; Russia filed suit in the EU General Court on 8 Sept 2026 to annul the freeze (kohenavocats.com, 13 Sept 2026).
weaponization_event.rationale: The BRICS Pay formal summit launch is a new non-dollar settlement agreement/launch — Band 1 by the rubric. The EU indefinite freeze is an escalation of the existing 2022 freeze, not a new completed sovereign seizure (title has not transferred), so it does not meet the Band 2 threshold of a new reserve freeze/seizure or a major economy operationally moving reserve settlement off USD.

dissent.view: Some sources (watcher.guru, informedclearly.com) characterise BRICS Pay as already 'operational' with intra-bloc USD usage sharply reduced, which could argue for Band 2 if one reads it as a major economy operationally moving reserve settlement off USD; however these sources are lower-authority aggregators and BIS/official data still show USD on one side of ~89% of FX turnover.

The EU's Dec 12 2025 indefinite-freeze Council decision has been characterised by Fair Observer and Modern Diplomacy as a shift 'from temporary sanctions to potentially permanent seizure,' which some analysts read as meeting a Band 2 threshold; however legal title has not transferred and actual confiscation has not been executed.

insurer_exits.fact: ClimateCosmos (June 2026) identifies 13 US states with active home-insurer non-renewal waves in 2026, including CA, FL, LA, TX, CO, GA, OK, and NE; corroborated by RollingOut (Sep 5 2026) and NAIC-sourced data showing FL non-renewal rate of 3.35% and CA at 3.18% (2024, per leadgen-economy.com June 2026). State Farm not writing new policies in CA, MA, RI (US News Sep 2026); Farmers absent from FL, HI, and 8 other states. AM Best upgraded homeowners segment outlook from negative to stable Dec 2025, and FL Citizens fell from 1.42M to ~390K policies by Jan 2026, indicating partial stabilization in some markets.
insurer_exits.rationale: 13 confirmed states with active non-renewal waves places the indicator squarely in the 5-15 state 'RISING' band (rubric score 1); no evidence of a confirmed full top-10 insurer exit from a major state market in 2026 itself, and AM Best's stable outlook plus FL Citizens contraction signals some markets are stabilizing rather than accelerating.

dissent.view: ClimateCosmos (non-authoritative, AI-adjacent content site) lists 13 states but without DOI or AM Best citation; the DOI/AM Best primary anchor is indirect via NAIC 2024 data with a 12-month lag, so the true 2026 count could differ.
AM Best upgraded homeowners P&C market outlook to stable in Dec 2025, suggesting the withdrawal wave may be past its peak rather than still 'rising'.

cat_losses.fact: Global insured nat cat losses totaled ~$42-47bn in H1 2026, the lowest H1 since 2018-2020 and 16-28% BELOW the 10-year average (Swiss Re: $42bn vs. trend of $66bn, 16% below; Gallagher Re: $46bn vs. 10y avg $64bn, 28% below; Munich Re: $44bn vs. 10y avg $50bn); the largest single H1 event was ~$5.8bn insured (April SCS outbreak). No Q3 2026 major hurricane or wildfire event exceeding $10bn in insured losses has been reported as of September 14, 2026. Sources: Swiss Re Institute (Aug 2026), Munich Re H1 nat cat report (Jul 30 2026), Aon Global Cat Recap H1 2026 (Jul 22 2026), Gallagher Re H1 2026 Nat Cat Report (Jul 2026).
cat_losses.rationale: H1 2026 YTD insured losses are well below the 10-year average across all three primary sources, and no single event has crossed the $10bn insured-loss threshold; both rubric conditions for ELEVATED (score=1) are unmet. Hurricane season remains subdued under El Nino and no Q3 event >$10bn has been reported, keeping the indicator at NORMAL (score=0).

ss_reform_news.fact: The 2026 SSA Trustees Report (issued June 9, 2026) projects the OASI trust fund depleted in Q4 2032 -- one quarter earlier than the 2025 report -- with the 75-year actuarial deficit widening to 4.42% of taxable payroll (source: ssa.gov/oact/trsum/, June 2026). No benefit cut has been enacted; Congress is debating but has not passed the Bipartisan Social Security Commission Act of 2026 (H.R. 9187) or the PROMISE Act (S. 4979).
ss_reform_news.rationale: The trustees report materially worsened the OASI depletion date and the long-term funding gap, and reform legislation is actively debated in both chambers -- satisfying the rubric's DEBATE criterion (band 1). No automatic cut has been triggered (trust fund not yet depleted) and no legislation enacting cuts has been enacted, so band 2 is not met.

pension_leverage_event.fact: ESMA June 2026 stress-test paper (esma.europa.eu, pub. June 2026) finds LDI fund liquidity shortfall under stress fell from EUR 9bn to EUR 3bn by end-2024; TPR market-oversight report (thepensionsregulator.gov.uk, data to March 2025) confirms LDI market shrank from ~GBP 1.5tn to ~GBP 0.7tn, rate buffers raised to ~300 bps, and daily volatility in leveraged LDI assets is >50% lower than end-2021. No forced gilt selling, margin blowup, or central-bank intervention has been reported in 2026.
pension_leverage_event.rationale: Both TPR and ESMA confirm materially improved buffers, lower leverage, and no active margin-stress episode in 2026; the rubric condition for score 0 (LDI buffers adequate, no margin stress, cited by TPR/ESMA) is satisfied. ESMA notes a residual tail risk for a subset of funds under a large shock, but this is a structural caveat in a stress-test paper, not an active regulatory flag of stress, so it does not elevate the score to 1.

dissent.view: ESMA (June 2026) notes that 'a subset of funds might still face challenges in meeting liquidity demands in case of a large interest rate shock', representing a residual vulnerability not fully captured by a score of 0.

funded_ratio.fact: Milliman 100 Public Pension Funding Index (PPFI): the funded ratio of the 100 largest U.S. public pension plans was 88.2% as of July 31, 2026, down from 88.7% as of June 30, 2026. Source: Milliman / BusinessWire, published August 27, 2026. https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20260827829119/en/Milliman-analysis-Public-pension-funded-ratio-slips-again-to-88.2-as-of-July-31
funded_ratio.rationale: The Milliman PPFI is the authoritative monthly mark-to-market index for the 100 largest U.S. public DB plans; 88.2% is the most recent published reading (July 31, 2026) and maps directly to the rubric's request for a representative large-plan funded ratio. Equable's FY2026 actuarial projection of 85.0% and NASRA median of ~73-75% are alternative measures on different methodological bases but are less current.

dissent.view: Equable Institute 'State of Pensions 2026' projects the national funded ratio at 85.0% for FY2026 (actuarial basis, 253 plans, best level since 2009)
NASRA median funded ratio approximately 73-75% for 2024-2025 (median across all public plans, broader universe, actuarial basis)

interconnection_months.fact: LBNL Queued Up 2026 Edition (June 2026, data through end of 2025): 'the median U.S. project that reached commercial operation in 2025 spent 61 months in the interconnection queue' (IR to COD); LBNL's own summary states 'median duration from IR to COD was over 5 years for projects built in 2025.' Source: emp.lbl.gov/queues; corroborated by axis-intelligence.com citing LBNL 2026 Edition.
interconnection_months.rationale: The rubric requests the latest LBNL median wait in months; the 2026 Edition (most recent, published June 2026) gives 61 months IR-to-COD for 2025 completions, directly mapping to the indicator. A secondary 45-month figure (IR to signed IA only) covers a narrower sub-milestone and is noted as a dissent.

dissent.view: 45 months median from interconnection request to signed interconnection agreement in 2025 per LBNL 2026 Edition — a sub-milestone, not full queue-to-COD duration

dc_moratoria.fact: New York Governor Kathy Hochul signed Executive Order 62 on July 14, 2026, creating the nation's first statewide data center moratorium — pausing state environmental permits for data centers ≥50 MW for up to one year (governor.ny.gov, July 14, 2026). Additionally, Texas Governor Abbott ordered a statewide grid audit in August 2026 effectively pausing new projects (multistate.us, Aug 19, 2026). DLA Piper (July 1, 2026) counts 56 public actions across 25 states and 100+ local moratoria enacted nationwide.
dc_moratoria.rationale: The rubric's Level 2 threshold requires 'a statewide moratorium enacted OR >10 jurisdictions with enacted pauses/cancellations.' New York's signed executive order alone clears the statewide bar; the 100+ local moratoria across 25 states independently clears the >10-jurisdiction bar. Both conditions are met simultaneously with confirmed physical permit blockages.

dissent.view: Maine's legislature passed a moratorium in April 2026, which would have been the first statewide enactment, but Gov. Janet Mills vetoed it — so Maine does not count as enacted.

New York's Responsible Data Center Development Act (S10642/A11560), passed by the legislature June 4, 2026, has not been signed into law by Hochul — the operative action is the July 14 executive order, not the statute.

ai_power_pressure.fact: As of end-2025/early-2026, U.S. interconnection queues held ~1,312 GW of generation + ~749 GW of storage across ~8,200 active projects (LBNL Queued Up 2026 Edition, emp.lbl.gov, data through end-2025); ERCOT alone received 198 GW of large-load applications in Q1 2026, with data centers comprising ~87% of ERCOT's 410 GW large-load queue; interconnection wait times in the busiest U.S. markets run 4-7 years. FERC on 18 June 2026 issued emergency orders to all six regional grid operators to accelerate large-load interconnection, explicitly citing unprecedented data-center-driven demand backlogs. No confirmed forced curtailment of data-center load or declared grid emergency has been reported.
ai_power_pressure.rationale: Queues are massive, lengthening, and causing multi-year project delays for power - squarely matching rubric band 1 (TIGHT). FERC's June 2026 emergency action confirms the severity, but the absence of any confirmed curtailment of data-center load or a declared grid emergency prevents escalation to band 2 (ACUTE).

dissent.view: Some secondary sources cite 2,600 GW in total U.S. queues as of early 2026, likely combining generation, storage, and large-load requests across all queue types, versus LBNL's more conservative 1,312 GW generation + 749 GW storage figure based on ISO/RTO filings through end-2025.

mine_disruptions.fact: Three top-20 copper mines have confirmed, ongoing production cuts active in 2026: (1) Grasberg (Indonesia, #2 globally) — Freeport-McMoRan declared force majeure after Sep 8 2025 mudslide, 2026 output cut ~35% to ~500kt vs prior 730kt guidance, full recovery deferred to 2028 (Benchmark Minerals / Crux Investor, Mar 2026); (2) Kamoa-Kakula (DRC, top-5) — recovering from 2025 floods, 2026 guidance 380–420kt vs original 520–580kt, Q2 2026 output only 64,328t (Ivanhoe Mines press release, Jul 8 2026); (3) El Teniente (Chile, Codelco, top-10) — July 2025 rock burst still trimming ~25,000t from 2026 output (InvestorIdeas/Oregon Group, Feb 2026). Goldman Sachs slashed its global mine supply estimate by 350,000t for ongoing Grasberg and Kamoa-Kakula disruptions; Morgan Stanley projects a 600,000t 2026 deficit (Crux Investor, 2026).
mine_disruptions.rationale: Three named top-20 mines have confirmed, measurable production cuts active in 2026, exceeding the >=3-mine threshold for a CLUSTER; additionally, multiple major institutions explicitly forecast a 2026 copper market deficit attributable to these disruptions, satisfying the alternate rubric criterion. Rating = 2.

dissent.view: ICSG projects a modest 96,000t refined copper surplus for 2026, a more conservative read than the deficit forecasts from Goldman, Morgan Stanley and Benchmark — suggesting the net balance may be tighter than a deficit but not yet clearly negative.

copper_deficit_timing.fact: ICSG April 2026 Copper Market Forecast: global refined copper market surplus of ~96,000 metric tons in 2026, reversing the prior October 2025 forecast of a 150,000 mt deficit; driven by weaker demand growth (revised to 1.6% from 2.1%) and higher secondary/scrap output. Source: ICSG Copper Market Forecast 2026/2027, reported by admis.com (April 24, 2026), recyclingtoday.com (April 28, 2026), indexbox.io (April 25, 2026).
copper_deficit_timing.rationale: The ICSG's latest (April 2026) official forecast is a +96,000 mt surplus for 2026, which exceeds the +100kt surplus threshold in the rubric and maps mechanically to band 0 (SURPLUS). The prior October 2025 deficit forecast of -150,000 mt has been formally reversed.

dissent.view: ICSG October 2025 forecast projected a 150,000 mt refined copper DEFICIT for 2026, citing constrained concentrate supply; this was the prevailing view through early 2026
J.P. Morgan projected an even steeper 330,000 mt deficit for 2026, driven by AI/data-center demand

drought_chip_farm.fact: U.S. Drought Monitor (droughtmonitor.unl.edu, data valid Sept 8 2026): New Mexico shows 29.61% of state area in D3 (Extreme Drought) and 55.02% in D2 or worse; nationally 8.1% of CONUS is in D3 and 1.5% in D4, concentrated in the interior West/Southwest. No confirmed fab production curtailment found for 2026 Taiwan or US Southwest.
drought_chip_farm.rationale: D3 (Extreme Drought) covering ~30% of New Mexico meets the rubric's ACUTE threshold of 'extreme/exceptional (D3-D4)' for a named chip/agri hub in the US Southwest; the Taiwan signal is warning-level only (TSMC CEO comments, no confirmed curtailment) so the US Southwest D3 reading is the load-bearing trigger.

dissent.view: NCEI (Sept 1 2026) notes drought improvement expected for parts of the Southwest in September, and monsoon activity provided some relief to Arizona specifically; Arizona D3 coverage was only ~1.47% as of late June, far below New Mexico's 29.61%.
Taiwan water risk is a concern flagged by TSMC CEO (June 2026) but no current drought emergency or rationing order confirmed for 2026, making Taiwan alone insufficient for a score of 2.

reservoir_stress.fact: Lake Mead elevation 1,038.93 ft, storage 6,904,200 AF = 26.4% of 26,120,000 AF capacity, per U.S. Bureau of Reclamation daily gauge data (via ReservoirBench.com, sourced from USBR, September 8 2026). This is within 0.11 ft of the all-time record low of 1,038.82 ft set September 1 2026, and is already below Hoover Dam minimum power pool (~1,050 ft).
reservoir_stress.rationale: At 26.4% of capacity, Lake Mead is well below the rubric's 30% CRITICAL threshold; it is also approximately 11 ft below the Hoover Dam minimum power pool elevation (~1,050 ft), confirming a confirmed physical impact on hydropower generation — both conditions independently trigger score 2.

dissent.view: ColoradoRiverMonitor reports 28.5% capacity as of 9/14/2026 (7.45M AF current storage vs 26.13M AF max), a slightly higher reading likely due to a different capacity basis or a short-term uptick

water_dispute.fact: India has held the 1960 Indus Waters Treaty 'in abeyance' since April 2025 and continues to do so as of September 2026. On 31 August 2026, the Permanent Court of Arbitration at The Hague ruled the treaty 'remains fully in force' and India has no right to suspend it; India rejected the award as 'null and void' and reaffirmed the abeyance. Pakistan has stopped receiving routine river-flow data and site inspections since 2023; the Permanent Indus Commission has not met since May 2022. Pakistan's defence minister warned in June 2026 that water is a national security issue but said current developments do not yet warrant military action. No confirmed deliberate physical flow cut-off has been carried out. (Sources: Al Jazeera 2026-09-01, CNBC 2026-09-01, Britannica updated 2026-09-12, Chatham House 2026-04-17)
water_dispute.rationale: The Indus Waters Treaty is formally contested/suspended (held 'in abeyance' by India, rejected by The Hague, with official war threats exchanged in June 2026), satisfying rubric level 1 (treaty suspended/contested, official threats exchanged, no kinetic action). No confirmed deliberate physical flow cut-off has been carried out, so level 2 is not warranted.

dissent.view: GERD/Nile dispute also sits at level 1: diplomacy frozen, Egypt raising issue at UNSC, Ethiopia announcing three new Blue Nile dams in March 2026, but no kinetic action or confirmed flow cut-off (New Arab, JURIST April 2026)

fao_food_trend.fact: FAO FFPI averaged 133.3 points in August 2026, up 1.9% MoM from revised July level of 130.8 and +2.5% YoY, reaching its highest level since late 2022. Source: FAO newsroom (fao.org), released 4 September 2026.
fao_food_trend.rationale: Index is rising and at a multi-year high, but the MoM gain (+1.9%) is below the 3% upper bound for Band 1; the 3-month rise (~May 130.7 to Aug 133.3, ~+2%) is far below the 10% SPIKING threshold. Rubric maps squarely to ELEVATED (1).

china_export_curbs.fact: NDRC convened Dec 11 2025 meeting suspending phosphate (DAP/MAP/NPK) exports through August 31 2026; urea 2026 full-year export quota capped at 3.3Mt with $660/t FOB price floor, down from ~5Mt in 2025; as of July 29 2026 FertilizerDaily confirmed phosphate curbs extended through August 2026 and discoveryalert.com (dated ~Sep 10 2026) still characterises urea quota as the dominant live supply constraint - no confirmed post-Aug 31 formal lifting of phosphate ban found. Sources: Exiger/NDRC (Dec 2025), FertilizerDaily (Jul 29 2026), Profercy (May 26 2026), discoveryalert.com (Sep 2026).
china_export_curbs.rationale: Active phosphate suspension (NDRC-backed, through Aug 31) and a tightened urea volume cap with FOB price floor are confirmed in place; the most recent broadening (March 2026 NK-blend expansion) falls outside the trailing 3-month window (post-Jun 14), and no new product additions or quota reductions in Jun-Sep 2026 are confirmed, so rubric maps to 1 (IN PLACE) rather than 2.

hormuz_fertilizer.fact: WTO-AXSMarine Strait of Hormuz Trade Tracker (cited by ukragroconsult.com, ~12 Sep 2026): 'Fertilizer shipments through the Strait of Hormuz remained near zero in early September 2026'; straits.live (14 Sep 2026) confirms strait 'effectively closed to commercial shipping' with 6 transits on 2026-09-06 vs ~85/day baseline, and Brent crude at $107.72.
hormuz_fertilizer.rationale: Fertilizer/sulfur/ammonia flows through Hormuz are near zero per the WTO-AXSMarine tracker as of early September 2026, fully consistent with the strait being rated CLOSED (effectively 2); the rubric's required market corroboration is met by Brent crude elevated at ~$107.72, well above pre-crisis norms, confirming the physical disruption.

dissent.view: carraglobe.com notes that convoys are moving under naval escort and some tankers transit with AIS off, suggesting true flow may be 'somewhat higher' than 10 vessels/day reported by IMF PortWatch on 23 July - implying a possible floor above zero that could argue for a '1' if escort volumes are material

taiwan_tension.fact: ISW/AEI China & Taiwan Update (Sept 1, 2026): PLA carried out 125 aerial incursions into Taiwan's ADIZ in August 2026 — less than half the August 2024/2025 totals — while Taiwan's CGA recorded a record 244 PRC vessels in Taiwanese waters in July and 1,247 PRC vessels near Taiwan and its outlying islands since May 2026, with the PRC conducting persistent patrols east of Taiwan since May. The most recent named drill event was a two-day PLA live-fire exercise in the Taiwan Strait (Jul 24-25, 2026, per SCMP/MSA navigation warning). No kinetic clash or actual blockade has been reported.
taiwan_tension.rationale: Persistent PRC coast guard and naval patrols at record vessel counts plus a live-fire drill in July 2026 constitute assertive, large-scale pressure short of a kinetic clash or blockade, squarely matching rubric level 1 (ELEVATED). Aerial ADIZ incursions are trending down from 2024-2025 peaks, providing no market-disruption or blockade signal to support a level-2 read.

export_controls.fact: MATCH Act (introduced April 2, 2026) remains in congressional review targeting ASML DUV sales and servicing to China; China enacted 'Regulations on Industrial Chain and Supply Chain Security' in April 2026 (CSIS, April 17, 2026) and maintains rare earth export licensing controls (holmium, thulium, ytterbium) as active countermeasures. US Commerce Secretary Lutnick privately pressed ASML executives from April 2026 onward over alleged EUV diversion (Asia Times, July 11, 2026). Sources: CSIS (csis.org/analysis/new-momentum-old-problems, June 11 2026); Asia Times (July 11, 2026); TechPowerUp (Aug 2026).
export_controls.rationale: Both sides have enacted or sustained formal measures in the trailing window: the US legislative MATCH Act escalation targeting ASML DUV/servicing plus executive-branch pressure on ASML (TIGHTENING), and China's April 2026 supply-chain security regulations plus rare-earth export controls constitute documented formal countermeasures (RETALIATION), satisfying rubric level 2. Confidence is medium rather than high because the MATCH Act has not yet been enacted into law and no new BIS Federal Register rule issued in the strict trailing 3-month window was found.

dissent.view: MATCH Act is still a bill, not a final BIS rule — no new Federal Register export control measure was issued specifically in June-Sept 2026, which could support rating of 1 (TIGHTENING) rather than 2 if China's April 2026 supply-chain regulations are deemed pre-period or non-semiconductor-specific
ASML CFO downplayed rare-earth control impact and China revenue remained ~20% of 2026 sales, suggesting market signals do not fully corroborate a severe disruption at level 2

fab_concentration.fact: As of Q3 2026, TSMC's entire <=3nm capacity (~260,000+ wpm combined 2nm+3nm) is in Taiwan. Arizona Fab 21 Phase 1 runs 4nm; Phase 2 (3nm) began equipment installation July-Sept 2026 targeting 2H 2027 volume production. Japan Kumamoto Phase 2 (3nm) targets 2028. TSMC 2025 Annual Report (investor.tsmc.com) confirms 2nm ramping 'at both Hsinchu and Kaohsiung sites in Taiwan'; TrendForce/TechTimes (Aug 8 2026) puts combined 2nm+3nm at ~260,000 wpm in Q4 2026, all Taiwan. ~0% of operational <=3nm capacity is outside Taiwan.
fab_concentration.rationale: Zero operational overseas <=3nm fab exists today and offshore share is effectively 0%, well below the <10% threshold; this maps unambiguously to rubric level 2 (EXTREME). The only overseas <=3nm fabs (Arizona Phase 2, Kumamoto Phase 2) are in equipment-install or construction phase with volume production 1-2 years away.

dissent.view: TSMC CEO CC Wei stated in July 2025 Q2 earnings that TSMC aims to produce '30% of high-end chips in the US' via Arizona build-out — interpreted by some as near-term diversification underway; however this is a multi-year target (~2030) for planned capacity, not current operational output.
One analyst projection estimates sub-2nm capacity will split '70% Taiwan and 30% US by 2030' — a forward projection, not a 2026 figure.

hormuz_redsea_status.fact: IMF PortWatch recorded 6 transits on 2026-09-06 vs a pre-crisis baseline of ~85/day (straits.live, 2026-09-14); Brent crude stood at ~$108-110/bbl on 2026-09-14, up ~60-64% year-on-year (TradingEconomics / Fortune, 2026-09-14). The Strait of Hormuz has been effectively closed to commercial shipping since 28 Feb 2026 following the US-Israel air campaign on Iran; Iran declared it closed to 'unfriendly nations' and laid sea mines (Wikipedia / straits.live). Houthis simultaneously seized Greater and Lesser Hanish islands on 2026-09-14, tightening their grip on Bab el-Mandeb / Red Sea (Washington Times / AP, 2026-09-14).
hormuz_redsea_status.rationale: Transit volume at ~7% of baseline (6 vs ~85 ships/day) is well below the rubric's 25% threshold for closure, and Brent at ~$108-110/bbl — up ~60% YoY — provides the required corroborating market signal; no functioning convoy workaround or signed truce is in place (GCC-Iran talks were postponed by Tehran), satisfying all conditions for a score of 2.

dissent.view: A brief ceasefire framework in April 2026 and periodic GCC-Iran diplomatic contacts could arguaby cap the rating at 1 (contested), but Iran postponed the Oman talks and the strait remains physically blocked with no operational convoy system running.

cable_incidents.fact: The PEACE subsea cable was cut in the Red Sea at a location ~1,450km from Zafarnaat, Egypt; cause unknown; repair expected to take 'several months' due to cable ship capacity crunch -- Data Center Dynamics, 2026-07-27 (https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/peace-subsea-cable-cut-in-the-red-sea-repair-to-take-months/). As of 2026-09-14 no repair-completion notice has been found, making the outage likely still active (~7 weeks post-cut).
cable_incidents.rationale: A named major cable (PEACE) is confirmed severed in the Red Sea with a multi-month repair timeline; no completion signal found, satisfying rubric level 2 ('>=1 major cable currently severed and unrepaired'). Confidence is medium rather than high because no post-July source explicitly confirms the cable remains unrepaired on the assessment date.

dissent.view: The August 2026 dual-cable faults off Perth, Australia may also qualify as simultaneous cuts (rubric level 2), but cause and repair status are unconfirmed and location is outside Red Sea/Hormuz/Baltic scope.
Hormuz cables face elevated threat (IRGC regulatory proposals, May 2026) but no confirmed cut has been reported, consistent with rubric level 1 at most for that corridor.

treasury_clearing_rollout.fact: DTCC/FICC July 2026 readiness survey (sent to all GSD Netting Members) found most respondents 'already prepared or actively completing final readiness activities,' with 79% having required FICC account structures in place and ~$1.2T/day already clearing, but ~$300-400B/day cash still to be onboarded; TBAC May 2026 charge identified 'the largest challenge from an implementation standpoint continues to be the amount of legal work and documentation associated with the bilateral agreements'; SEC August 7 2026 statement (sec.gov) confirmed a 15c3-3 net-omnibus-margin exemptive relief request still open for comment (due Aug 31 2026) and SIFMA/IIB inter-affiliate exemptive relief requests still pending. No further deadline extension has been announced. Primary sources: DTCC/Finadium July 27 2026 (finadium.com/ficc-survey-shows-ust-clearing-at-scale-ahead-of-sec-deadline/); TBAC Charge Q2 2026 (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/TBACCharge1Q22026.pdf); SEC Uyeda statement Aug 7 2026 (sec.gov/newsroom/speeches-statements/uyeda-statement-update-secs-work-toward-treasury-clearing-implementation-080726).
treasury_clearing_rollout.rationale: No deadline extension has been granted (ruling out score 2), but a documented legal/documentation backlog for bilateral repo agreements plus multiple pending exemptive relief requests (SIFMA inter-affiliate, IIB cross-border, 15c3-3 net omnibus margin) squarely satisfy the rubric definition of FRICTION: documentation backlog and pending exemptive relief. Cash side is better positioned but repo readiness remains materially incomplete with $300-400B still to migrate on cash alone. [vintage guard: new read is 2026-08-07 data but the prior applied value was 2026-08 data; kept the newer vintage]

dissent.view: DTCC/FICC and SEC chair Atkins (March 2026) characterize the industry as 'well positioned' for the Dec 31 2026 cash deadline, suggesting a possible score of 0 for cash-specific readiness; however repo documentation backlog and open regulatory relief requests prevent a clean 'smooth' reading.
